description.value: The study investigated valence-dependent changes in effective connectivity within a right-hemisphere prefrontal-amygdala-fusiform face processing network during dynamic facial affect processing.

design.value: Thirty-three healthy volunteers completed a 6-min event-related fMRI dynamic face-matching and shape-matching task with positive, negative, and neutral facial-valence blocks. Whole-brain GLM analyses and dynamic causal modeling with Bayesian model comparison and Bayesian model averaging were performed.

medical_condition.value: healthy volunteers; no subject reported any past or current psychiatric disorder

task_description.value: Participants matched a dynamic target image with one of two static probe images according to facial emotion or number of vertices. The task comprised 12 alternating 20-s blocks, six face and six shape blocks, each containing five 4-s trials.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to match either the left or the right static item at the bottom with the dynamic item on top and to press either the left or the right button with their dominant hand on a response-pad to indicate their choice as soon as they recognized which probe matched.

stimuli.value: Dynamic and static emotional faces from the Radboud face database and polygon shapes. Positive blocks used happy, surprised, and neutral faces; negative blocks used sad and disgusted faces; neutral blocks used neutral and surprised faces.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3 Tesla scanner (Philips Medical Systems) using a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Functional images were acquired with a multiband echoplanar images (EPIs) sequence. Five dummy scans were acquired before the actual data acquisition.
